$comment: Dependency license policy (scripts/ci/check-licenses.mjs). Every production dependency must be covered by 'allowed'; a package whose SPDX expression names a license under 'denied', or a license listed nowhere, fails CI. An 'A OR B' expression passes when one alternative is allowed (that one is elected), 'A AND B' needs both. The packages under ee/ must additionally have copyleft 'none', so a license with copyleft 'file' or 'font' is not allowed there. A package with a wrong or missing license field whose license was checked by hand goes under 'overrides' as "name@version": {"license": "<SPDX expression>", "reason": "..."}; the entry applies to that exact version only. Third-party programs that Restow redistributes as separate binaries are checked module by module under 'redistributedBinaries' (the Go modules compiled into restic, licenses/restic-deps/modules.json): every module needs a license of 'allowed' with copyleft 'none', or an entry under that binary's 'exceptions'; such an exception allows nothing for Restow's own dependencies and nothing in ee/.

MIT.reason: Permissive; the large majority of the npm dependencies.

BSD-2-Clause.reason: Permissive; also the license of restic, which ships as a separate binary.

BSD-3-Clause.reason: Permissive; also the license of the Go standard library linked into the agent.

Apache-2.0.reason: Permissive with a patent grant; the license of the Restow core itself. NOTICE files of shipped Apache-2.0 dependencies are reproduced in NOTICE.

MPL-2.0.reason: Weak, file-level copyleft: accepted in the core for unmodified npm dependencies (today only lightningcss, an optional peer of the build tooling that is not used at run time); modified MPL files would have to be published under the MPL. Not allowed in ee/. The MPL-2.0 module inside the redistributed restic binary is allowed separately, by name, under 'redistributedBinaries'.

OFL-1.1.reason: SIL Open Font License for font files: accepted in the core for the font packages the web app bundles and serves itself (@fontsource/inter-tight and @fontsource/ibm-plex-mono, the typefaces of the brand guide); the copyright notices and license text ship in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md. A derived font must stay under the OFL, so it is not allowed in ee/.

MIT-0.reason: MIT without the attribution condition (nodemailer, smtp-server).

BlueOak-1.0.0.reason: Permissive with a patent grant (isexe, jackspeak, minipass, path-scurry, package-json-from-dist).

denied.GPL: Strong copyleft: the combined work would have to be released under the GPL.
denied.LGPL: Library copyleft: relinking and replacement duties that a bundled web app and a container image cannot meet cleanly.
denied.AGPL: Network copyleft: it would reach every installation that offers Restow over a network.
denied.SSPL: Server Side Public License: not an open-source license, it demands the source of the whole service stack.
denied.EUPL: Copyleft. A dual-licensed package that offers a permissive alternative (for example MIT OR EUPL-1.1+) is accepted under that alternative.

separateWorks.$comment: Folders of this repository that are separate works under their own license, not part of the Apache-2.0 core (scripts/ci/check-separate-works.mjs). Each carries its full license text and SPDX headers, holds no Restow core code, is referenced only from the files listed under 'allowedReferences' and is copied nowhere else. Nothing here allows that license for dependencies of the core or of ee/.

integrations/pve/plugin.reason: The storage plugin shim for Proxmox VE (maintainer decision 2026-10-03, docs/PROXMOX.md 2.2): Perl modules that PVE loads into its own daemons and that derive from PVE::Storage::Plugin and PVE::BackupProvider::Plugin::Base, which are AGPL-3+. The shim only receives PVE's calls and runs the separate program restow-pve (Apache-2.0, agent/cmd/restow-pve) with JSON on stdin and stdout (docs/PVE-PROTOCOL.md); it contains no Restow logic. It ships as source, with its LICENSE, next to restow-pve in the linux-amd64 agent release.

redistributedBinaries.$comment: Programs Restow ships unmodified as separate binaries, in the images and to every endpoint, with the Go modules compiled into them. 'modules' is the vendored list (scripts/restic-licenses.mjs, checked against the pinned binaries in CI). A module passes with a license of 'allowed' whose copyleft is 'none', or when it is named under 'exceptions' with exactly the license it has. An exception covers that module inside that binary only.

github.com/hashicorp/golang-lru/v2.reason: An LRU cache that restic uses, compiled unmodified into its release binary (restic 0.19.1: v2.0.7). MPL-2.0 is file-level copyleft: the executable may be passed on under any terms as long as its recipients are told where the source code of the MPL-covered files is (MPL 2.0, section 3.2); THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and agent/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt say so in the module's entry. Allowed for this module in the restic binary only, never for Restow's own dependencies and never in ee/.
